chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ja'far ibn Yunus, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, who said:

We were in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and I counted in the room fourteen men. So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) sneezed, and no one from the group spoke. So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Are you not saying the Tasmit? Are you not saying the Tasmit? From the rights of the believer upon the believer is that when he is sick, you visit him, and when he dies, you attend his funeral, and when he sneezes, you say the Tasmit (or he said: You say the Tashmit), and when he invites you, you answer him.'

key_terms.تَسْمِيتٌ: The act of saying 'Alhamdulillah' after someone sneezes.
key_terms.تَشْمِيتٌ: The act of saying 'Yarhamuk Allah' (May Allah have mercy on you) after someone sneezes.

ai.seo_question: What are the rights of a believer upon another according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: Imam Jaafar al-Sadiq (AS) uses this incident to define 'Tashmit' (responding to a sneeze with 'Yarhamukallah') as a fundamental social right (Haqq) of the believer, linking it directly to other key acts of solidarity like visiting the sick and attending funerals. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on communal etiquette as a manifestation of faith, where minor social interactions reinforce the bonds of brotherhood and mutual responsibility within the Ummah.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ja’far Bin Yunus, from Dawood Bin Al Husayn who said,

‘We were in the presence of Abu Abdullahasws, and I counted in the room, there were fourteen men. So Abu Abdullahasws sneezed, and no one from the group spoke (a word)’. So Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Are you not Naming (Allahazwj)? Are you not Naming (Allahazwj)? From the rights of the Momin upon the Momin is that when he is sick, that you should visit him, and when he dies, that you should attend his funeral, and when he sneezes, that you should Name (Allahazwj)’. Or heasws said: ‘Yushammituhu’ (be glad for him)’, ‘And when he invites you, that you answer him’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Faddal from Ja’far ibn Yunus from Dawud ibn al-Hosayn who has said the following:

“Once we were in the presence of abu ‘Abd Allah, recipient of divine supreme covenant. I counted that the people present were fourteen. Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) sneezed and no one from the people said anything. Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) then asked, ‘You did not respond. Why did you not respond? It is of the rights of a believing person on the other believing person to visit him in his illness, attend his funeral, and respond to his sneezing, or he said, yusammithu (response to his sneezing) and when he invites accept his invitation.’”
